title: Onset of Ergodicity Across Scales on a Digital Quantum Processor
abstract: Studies onset of ergodicity in a 2D disordered Heisenberg Floquet model using digital quantum simulation on IBM's Nighthawk 120-qubit superconducting processor (ibm_miami), reaching system sizes up to 10x10=100 qubits. Probes ergodicity across length scales via coarse-grained collision entropy patches up to 3x3. Finds smooth crossover from subergodic to ergodic behavior as coupling J increases, with smaller patches thermalizing first. In regimes where tensor-network simulations are reliable, excellent agreement with error-mitigated quantum simulation. Beyond this regime, volume-law entanglement causes classical cost to rise sharply.
key_claims: 100-qubit (10x10) quantum simulation of 2D Heisenberg Floquet model on IBM Nighthawk
Hierarchy of ergodicity across scales: smaller patches thermalize first
Classical tensor-network simulations agree with quantum results in tractable regime
Quantum simulation accesses volume-law entanglement regime beyond classical reach
Error-mitigated results validated against tensor-network benchmarks
